text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- IPEA SAYS CARS ENJOY 270 PCT PROTECTION

A study by Brazil's Research Institute for Applied Economics (Ipea) says measures protecting domestic industry are effectively increasing more than import tariffs. Cars, buses and trucks saw protection rise to 270 percent in 1995 from 44.6 percent in 1994, while import tariffs only rose to 55.5 percent from 19.9 percent.
-- AUTOPART FIRMS NEED TO INVEST $5 BLN

Brazilian autopart firms will have to invest at least $5 billion in modernizing their factories if they want to keep up with carmakers who have promised new investments of $13 billion in Brazil until the year 2000.
-- CIVIL SERVANT WHO RESIGNS TO EARN 1.8 PCT OF SALARY
The federal government is to announce today its voluntary redundancy program which will pay public workers between 1.2 and 1.8 percent of their salary for each year of service.
-- GOVT TO AUCTION POSSESSIONS CONFISCATED DURING THE WAR

The government will auction off possessions worth 46 million reais it has discovered in the Central Bank and the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange which once belonged to Germans, Italians and Japanese and were confiscated during the Second World War.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has dismissed senate opposition to the privatization of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), reaffirming the company would be sold off in 1997.
-- GOALKEEPER SUFFERS BRAIN BLOODCLOT IN ATTACK

Goalkeeper Ricardo Pinto of soccer team Atletico-PR has been hospitalized with a bloodclot in his brain after fans of Rio de Janeiro's Fluminense soccer team attacked Atletico players on the weekend after a match in which Fluminense lost.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
